name: Utility Piping — Cooling, Steam, Air, Water and N2 Services
zones: underground utility runs and valve chambers

activities: spool fabrication (B31.1 for steam/power, water/GRP/HDPE for services)
buried line laying on bedding in trench
welded, flanged, grooved-coupling, HDPE butt-fusion or PVC solvent joints as service dictates
reduced scope vs process; RT for steam/power lines, mostly VT for water; fusion-joint records for non-metallic
hydrotest; buried lines tested before backfill
target-plate steam blowing for steam lines
put utility header into service ahead of the process systems it feeds

typical_relationships.reason: buried pipe is laid on prepared bedding in an open, shored trench
a buried line cannot be inspected or leak-located once covered

typical_relationships.after: install above-ground utility mains on it
typical_relationships.reason: the rack carries the utility header; steel must be up and surveyed first
the joint must exist and be accepted before it can hold test pressure
debris and contamination must be cleared before a utility feeds equipment or is consumed
the line is proven for pressure before high-energy steam blowing to a target plate

typical_relationships.before: commission utility systems (cooling water, air, N2, steam)
typical_relationships.after: commission the process systems that consume them
typical_relationships.reason: process commissioning needs live utilities as prerequisites
the valve station is mounted in/on its chamber

interfaces.requirement: trenches, valve pits, thrust blocks, crossings and backfill/reinstatement coordinated with pipe laying and testing
pipe rack / sleeper steel erected before above-ground utility mains
utility headers commissioned before the process systems they feed
utilities (cooling, air, N2, steam) live to support equipment commissioning
flow meters and control valves on utility headers reinstated and calibrated
utility pumps energised; heat tracing on outdoor water lines before insulation
shared underground corridor and crossing coordination

testing_requirements: Hydrotest per B31.1 (steam/power) or water spec; buried lines tested before backfill
Steam blowing / target-plate cleanliness before connecting steam to turbines or equipment
Potable water disinfection/chlorination with bacteriological clearance
Non-metallic (HDPE/GRP/PVC) fusion/joint records in lieu of weld NDT
commissioning_dependencies: Utility source available (pump station, package unit, or tie-in to existing utility)
System flushed / disinfected / blown and certified clean
Utilities scheduled early in the commissioning sequence as prerequisites to process systems
Instrumentation and control on the utility header live
typical_exceptions: Non-metallic services have no weld NDT — fusion/joint records instead
Gravity drains tested by fill/flow rather than pressure
Temporary commissioning utilities (temp air/water/N2) precede permanent systems and support other commissioning
evidence: Utility headers (cooling water, instrument air, N2, steam) were flushed/blown and commissioned ahead of the process systems they feed, and buried utility runs were hydrotested before backfill because they cannot be inspected once covered.
